namespace LO.System

open LO.System.NegationEquiv LO.System.FiniteContext List

variable {F : Type*} [LogicalConnective F] [DecidableEq F] {S : Type*} [System F S] {𝓢 : S} [System.Minimal 𝓢]
  {φ ψ χ : F} {Γ Δ : List F}
informal_statement: Given an intuitionistic logic system �� equipped with the axiom of Double Negation Elimination (DNE), if �� proves either `¬¬φ` or `¬¬ψ`, then it must also prove `φ` or `ψ`, respectively.
informal_proof: We begin by considering the disjunction `¬¬φ ∨ ¬¬ψ`, which is known to be provable in the system ��. Since �� possesses the DNE axiom, we can immediately eliminate the double negations from each disjunct. This means we can derive `φ` from `¬¬φ` and `ψ` from `¬¬ψ`. By applying DNE to the disjunction, we obtain either `φ` or `ψ` as the conclusion, thereby completing the proof.

C1_dependencies.name: DecidableEq
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
Asserts that `α` has decidable equality, that is, `a = b` is decidable
for all `a b : α`. See `Decidable`.
-/
abbrev DecidableEq (α : Sort u) :=
  (a b : α) → Decidable (Eq a b)
